utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to the Prosecution, I'd like to provide you with some information. You'll be testifying under 92 -- under Rule 92 ter. The Prosecutor will ask you to identify a document that you have already signed and might show you some documents after having made a brief summary of your written statement. Once this has been done, and I believe that this should only take between 15 and 20 minutes, Defence counsel, who are to your left, may put questions to you as part of their cross-examination. So each Defence team will have 15 minutes, and if one Defence team doesn't want to use up their time they can give their time to another Defence team. As a rule, your testimony should be completed this morning. If you find that you have any difficulties, inform us of the fact. We'll have a break a little later on so that you can have a rest. We'll have a break at 10.30. Having said that, I'll now give the floor to Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness BX, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: We'll be referring today to you as Witness BX because you've been granted the protective measures. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness BX, I'm first going to read a summary of your statement, and then I'm going to ask you a few questions. The Witness, a Bosniak woman, was residing with her family in Hrasnica in the municipality of Gornji Vakuf when the HVO soldiers started shelling Hrasnica sometime after the 5th of January, 1993. The shelling lasted for about seven days during which the civilians took shelter in the houses with cellars. Around mid-January, 1993, HVO soldiers entered the village, and the civilians and soldiers defending the village surrendered amidst insults and abuse. The elderly, women, and children were separated from the military-aged men, and everyone was made to walk to the village of Volari. While walking, she witnessed the HVO looting and setting houses on fire. The witness and two men got wounded by bursting bullets. At Volari, the approximate 150 civilians were put into a single bus and transported to a furniture factory in Trnovaca where they were kept for one night in harsh conditions. The civilians were then taken to three neighbouring Muslim houses. The owner of the house she stayed in was beaten by the HVO. She was allowed to go to Hrasnica for food under supervision, and she saw that the mosque in Hrasnica had been destroyed. After being kept for 21 days, she and the other 150 civilians were released. She found out that the men detained in the factory were taken to Prozor. Now, Witness, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions. Did you ever provide a written statement to the investigator -- to an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And when did you give this written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 13th of January, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at the time you provided this written statement, did you answer the questions to the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, nothing but truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you answer the questions freely, that is, without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At the conclusion of that interview, madam, was your statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you then sign that statement in the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm now going to provide you copies of both the English and the B/C/S version of your statement. Witness, could you take a look at both statements, and can you confirm that the version -- well, can you confirm that you actually signed the English version of the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is this the statement that was taken from you in January, 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you met with an investigator and myself. Do you recall that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at that point in time were you given an opportunity to review your statement in the Bosnian language again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, upon reviewing your statement, did you have any corrections to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were two matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Witness, if you can take your statement into the -- the statement in the Bosnian -- of your own language, and if you could have a look at that, and maybe if I could refer you to paragraph 10 of your statement. Can you explain to the Court what corrections you want to make in this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to correct something here. It says Sejo Guric. She [as interpreted] wasn't wounded by a shell. She was wounded by a bullet, since when we were captured, one soldier from the HVO approached them earlier on and said that one of theirs had died, and then two members of the HVO went to Sejo Guric and Asim Guric, and then Asim was seriously wounded, and Sejo Guric was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You say that Sejo Guric was killed. Do you know how Sejo Guric was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there were a number of us and were taken to the HVO. The HVO soldiers were there, and one of their men came and said that a soldier of theirs had been killed, and then two of them got angry. They set off towards Sejo and Asim Guric, and they were angry, and then one was wounded and the other person was killed. They used a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And you say one was wounded and the other was killed. And who was actually killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sejo Guric was killed. Asim Guric was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, madam. There was a question. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but there's a mistake in the transcript, and I believe it's important. On page 8, line 22 to 25. In the case of Sejo Guric, the word "she", the pronoun "she" is used but it's a man. So it should be "he". Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, given your answers, could we clarify something? You said the two inhabitants of the village were victims. One person was killed and another wounded. Given the description you have just provided us with -- well, did you see the event itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement you also made reference to another person, which is Muminovic, of which you don't the first name. In your statement -- your statement reads that this man was killed due to shelling. What do you know about Muminovic, and can you explain that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all I know is that he was killed. We weren't nearby. I don't know how this happened, but I know that at that time he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But you didn't see how he got killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you said that there were two corrections that you wanted to make to your statement. Is there anything else that you wanted to correct in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, besides the corrections that you -- that you've just explained to the Judges, is there -- is there anything else that you want to add or delete or correct to this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And I were to ask you questions now about the subject matters contained in your written statement, would your answer reflect what is written in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I would now like to show you a document, which is Exhibit P 01371. Witness, could you read out the heading of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "A list of individuals captured from Hrasnica, captured by HVO members."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like to ask you is whether you could go through this list and tell the Court whether you recognise the names on this list as the persons captured in Hrasnica in January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall whether the HVO was making up a list after the villages were captured? Do you recall that this was done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, going through the list, it appears that your name is not on this list. Do you know why you would not be on this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. We were refugees. Maybe that's why they didn't put us on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you say you were refugees, do you -- do you mean to say that you were not an origin habitant of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, I wasn't living in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. And as far as you can say, the names that appear on this list, are these all names of persons who actually originally inhabited in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you said that you were a refugee. Which was your place of origin? Where did you come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the municipality of Bugojno, but I lived in the village of Planinci. So I had to flee from there because this area was constantly under Serbian attack. So that's when I went to Hrasnica. I wasn't married.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us when exactly you arrived in the village of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But roughly speaking. Was it one or two or three months later, earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps a month before the conflict broke out in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, did you arrive there on your own or with your husband? What was your marital status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't married. I went there with my mother and my two brothers and my sister-in-law and their children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have any other exhibits to show to this witness, so I'm almost done. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos, the list that we have and which you are probably going to ask to be admitted, where does this document come from? Because when I see it in B/C/S, there's no stamp on it. There are handwritten notes. Where did you find this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, there is a stamp on the original B/C/S version, and the document does come from the Croatian archives. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it has the stamp of the archives that's another matter, but when I say there is no stamp officialising this document as coming from a source of the HVO unit or the municipal authority, there is an archive stamp apparently, but when it reached the archives it must have come from somewhere. Where did it come from this document? Or perhaps your investigator did not ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wouldn't be able to give you an answer to -- to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I ask the Prosecution to always ask the question of the origin of the document, where does this particular document come from, because a Judge may ask such a question. And in order to be able to judge the probative value of a document, it is necessary to have certain information. We see now that it comes from the archives, but apart from that nothing more. Please continue, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm -- I'm done with my examination-in-chief. I just want to introduce the statement of this witness as an exhibit, and that will be Exhibit P 09710, and we will have to admit it under seal because this witness is protected. And as for the exhibit that's been shown to her, Exhibit 01371, this exhibit has also been admitted through Witness BV. So I don't think I need to admit it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Judges have a few questions to ask before giving the floor to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You recognised the list of persons captured shown to you by the Prosecutor, but according to your statement, you arrived in Hrasnica in January, 1993, having come from a different village. My question would be: Do you recognise the people on this list that you knew or that you met upon your arrival in Hrasnica before these people were captured and detained, or did you come to know these people after their liberation? I'm asking this question to check your knowledge of this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew these people from before. I would come and visit my relatives before. I knew them all from earlier on, before their capture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what happened to them after they were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. They were separated from us. They were taken away from Trnovaca to Prozor. What happened to them after that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also have a question, but I shall give the floor first to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Madam, in your statement, it's the point number 10, you tell that the HVO entered the village, and then you say, "But the shelling continued," and you say that two Muslim men got killed due to the shelling. That is -- that is what you have corrected, is it not? You have corrected it with regard to Guric but not with regard to Muminovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see how Muminovic got killed, but I did see Sejo Guric and Asim Guric. I saw two men going towards them. I don't know exactly who they were, but I saw them, that they killed these two, or that they shot at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Would you -- would you still -- would you still say that Muminovic was killed due to the shelling, or is it your statement today that you do not know how he was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know for certain how he was killed. I know about these other two, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: How, then, do you know at all that Mr. Muminovic has been killed? Was that hearsay, others told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. His brother came when they transported us to Volari, and then he said that his brother had been killed. But this was only about 10 minutes later, but I wasn't present where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, consulting the list that you saw a moment ago, I noticed that this list has two components, one under the heading "Fighters," or "Soldiers," and the other "Civilians." In the village that you were in, were there soldiers, members of the Territorial Defence or the BH army, who were in the village? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. How many were there, roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I'm unable to answer that question as to the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The soldiers that you saw, were they carrying weapons, rifles? Did you see them walking around the village armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course they had rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I come to an important question. You said in your written statement that the shelling started around the 5th of January. According to your recollection, the armed inhabitants of the village, did they open fire at the HVO, or were they, like you, in the cellars, in the basements seeking shelter from the shells that were falling? Can you give us a little more information about the situation as you experienced it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation there was such that there was shooting with rifles and shelling. There were some soldiers in the cellars, but there were also some outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is important for us to know. You said that they were shooting. Who were they shooting at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, of course there was only the HVO. They had no one else to shoot at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That brings me to the end of my questions. You have explained that at a given moment, about 5.00 in the afternoon, HVO soldiers entered your village, and you described that their faces were painted, that they were dressed in black. And what is it that makes you say that these were members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came to that conclusion because I saw that only the HVO were there, because they had insignia on their sleeves, most of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's a point of clarification. You have just told us that they had insignia on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On one sleeve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, on one sleeve. Can you explain the insignia for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a kind of ribbon saying "HVO," and there was their mark on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This will be my last question now. The HVO soldier who fired at the person who was killed, Sejo Guric, did this soldier have the HVO sign on his sleeve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Asim Guric knew those people personally. I didn't. I just knew that they were from near Hrasnica, from the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that Guric knew these persons. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war there were a bar in the village, and they would come there, and they knew each other. But he couldn't probably immediately recognise him because his face was painted and he had a mask on his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say before the war, you mean before the 5th of January, or do you mean before the war in more general terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were neighbours. They knew each other for years. It wasn't just a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling me that the HVO soldiers whose insignia you saw were apparently quite certainly neighbours of the inhabitants of this village. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They were from nearby, the people who were with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My final question, because I could go on like this for hours, but I should stop. My last question. The HVO soldiers that you saw entering the village, were they under the command of a chief? Did you have the impression that there was a chief or a head controlling them, or did they just enter the village without any leader, or perhaps you can't answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question. All I know is that they entered the village, they told us to leave our houses, and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence now has an hour and a half for their questions, which means 15 minutes each.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Witness, good morning. I'm attorney from Zagreb, and I am the Defence counsel for General Milivoj Petkovic. I have a number of questions for you so as to -- so as we can understand better your statement. In your statement, you wrote that the shelling lasted about seven days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So one might conclude that the resistance of your army was quite fierce since you managed to resist the artillery of the HVO for all of seven days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Our people didn't believe that this would happen because we were all neighbours and nobody thought anything terrible would happen. The point was to scare the people a little. Nobody expected the combat to go on for so long.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying, but the fact is that according to what you said, the shelling of the village lasted seven days and a lot of shells fell on the village. One could come to the conclusion that your army's resistance was considerable, that your soldiers fought bravely to prevent the HVO soldiers entering the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They fought against them entering, but they didn't have any means for shelling or heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that the civilians hid in the cellars of houses. Could you tell us with greater detail where your soldiers were? How far away were they from the places where you were hiding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but they were not far from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at least roughly? When you say they weren't far, it could be 50 metres. Were they about 50 metres away, that is, the line of your soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know with precision, but that is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. You say you visited Hrasnica and that you knew the inhabitants there, so I assume you were also familiar with the roads around Hrasnica. Tell me, was Hrasnica village on a hill or in a valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the plain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was Hrasnica close to a road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where this road led to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Coming from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what about the road from Travnik and Novi Travnik towards Gornji Vakuf. Was it also close to Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. The witnesses who also recounted the events in Hrasnica mention the fact that a relatively large number of civilians from Hrasnica managed to escape. The civilians from central Hrasnica to upper Hrasnica, then the civilians from lower Hrasnica to other villages. Were you aware that some civilians had left the village and thus avoided the events that you have described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early in the morning some people who could -- there was a pedestrian bridge across the Vrbas River, and then some civilians managed to cross in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you know that they were leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were leaving. Some were hoping that there would be no serious difficulties and that it would pass quickly, so that most of us hoped that this would not come to much and we stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, was it your own decision or did somebody advise you to stay? How come that you stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed because I had family obligations. My mother and sister-in-law left with the children, and I had to look after the cattle, the livestock. So that is why I stayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you were the only one of your family who stayed. The others managed to escape, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that some houses were destroyed in the shelling. Was a house set on fire by the shells, any house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were those houses burning as a result of the shelling before the HVO entered the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your best recollection, do you know whether any shell damaged the mosque in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So, yes, one of the shells damaged the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know of any Croatian families from Hrasnica pillaging the houses of Muslims after you had left? Did you ever hear of any such cases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When they went for food, some people went before me. And when I went the last day to fetch food because we didn't have enough in the shelter, I saw them doing this myself. And other people told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you went to fetch food in your village, where did you find the food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The houses that were not totally destroyed. It didn't matter whose house it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see. So you collected food from the houses. According to what we know so far about the events in Hrasnica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. The Defence counsel has asked you a question which is important for us. Counsel asked you whether you knew of Croatian families stealing from Muslim houses. You said yes, but you said that they were doing what you were doing, going to fetch food. So I'm asking you to be more precise. Did Croats villagers go to Muslim houses to take food only or to steal TV sets, chairs, et cetera? Could you make this clearer for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't take food. They took furniture and household equipment, because I saw them loading cars with these things and leaving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So that was an important point. These Croats who were doing this, were they inhabitants of the village, or were they people or Croats coming from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were people from other locations, because there were only two Croat houses in that village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these were Croats coming from elsewhere. And they came with cars, carriages, trucks? What can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came with trucks and tractors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You just told us that there were only two Croat families. However, other witnesses from Hrasnica told us something else, so I wish to ask you, since after all, you were new in Hrasnica, are you quite sure that there were only two Croat families living in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In Hrasnica only two houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Including all parts of Hrasnica, Donja, Gornja, Srednja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I started asking you about the way you left the village. According to what we know so far, two columns were formed, one column consisting of soldiers, and another of civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how these two columns left the village? Which was the first to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which was the first. I just know which column I was in and that we were all civilians. As for the other column, I didn't see it. Some people left before us. We were not all kept in one house but in several places, and as people left these houses they headed towards Volari.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that all the civilians were in one column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in one column. We were transported to Volari in two groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that one column consisted of civilians and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know about the column I was in, and it consisted only of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me how long this column was approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how far from you were Asim and Sejo Guric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the number, but they were close by.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were they in front of you or behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went behind us, but we stopped there and I saw these two men approaching them and doing what they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So when these HVO soldiers headed towards them, the -- their part of the column continued but you stopped and turned around and watched. Was there some reason for you to stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stopped there. We didn't go any further. We stopped near a house to seek shelter. When we were captured, the shelling stopped, but there were only rifle shots. And this was right behind us, so we turned around, and the two were behind us when they did this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were these two at the end of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to Asim Guric about this event later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because I never saw Asim later. UNPROFOR took Asim to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 11, you said: "HVO soldiers in Trnovaca didn't take jewellery or other valuables"; is that right? So it means that you arrived in Trnovaca with your jewellery and valuables.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which -- so that in Hrasnica no HVO soldier took away from you your valuables; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they didn't take anything away.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also said in your statement that HVO soldiers told you that they would release you when they, the HVO, capture or take control of the village of Dolac. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is this village on the Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno road or on some other important road? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a village near Hrasnica, on the other side of the road, on the right-hand side. There's the Vrbas river and then the main road Bugojno-Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did they explain why they wouldn't release you before this operation of taking Dolac? Did they explain that they would keep you in Trnovaca for your own security for a while?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They didn't say anything else. In the evening when we reached Trnovaca, the furniture factory, they said that in the morning they would capture Dolac and then they would release us. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the HVO try to take control of the Dolac village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did the HVO succeed, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How come that they didn't succeed? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, because we were in Trnovaca at the time. So I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the BH army, or the Muslim army, or whatever you wish to call them, defended fiercely the village of Dolac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. They must have defended it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In view of what you told us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would like to have this clarified. You were asked whether you knew that Dolac was fiercely defended, and your answer was: "It must have been." So this is just an assumption you make, or do you know for sure? And if you know for sure, how come you know? Who told you? Why do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only assume that they must have done that. They must have defended it. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And my last question: Apart from the two villages that we have been discussing, villages where the ABiH and the HVO were fighting, do you know whether there were any other villages where those two armies were fighting so intensely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask you whether there is something you can remember. You said that the fighting started on the 5th of January. Do you remember the point at which it actually started? Do you remember how the fighting started, how the events started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly how all of this started, nor do I know when everything started exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you hear any guns opening fire? Did you hear shells falling, rifle shots? Because such events are events that one usually remembers. What I would like to know is how everything started on the 5th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, initially they only used light arms, and it grew more intensive later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say "they," who do you mean? "They used." Who used these weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that those who started the fighting were HVO members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now for the next Defence team? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And next Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. In light of the last few questions, I think I have a couple.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Ma'am, were you part of the -- of the Muslim army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have contact with the Muslim army to know what exactly they were up to, what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So on January 5th and prior to January 5th, you don't know to any degree of certainty what if anything the Muslim army was doing in that area, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't know whether they were initiating or engaging in any activities that might have provoked the HVO to respond?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when you said earlier to the Judge that it was the HVO that initiated the activities on January 5th, you really don't know. That's your assumption. Is it not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that the soldiers that you claimed to be HVO soldiers had painted faces so they could not be recognised; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you didn't recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No. How can the witness know why the HVO soldiers had painted their face. Soldiers paint their face so they are not seen in the night, and you give it a quite original interpretation of your own to just says this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Judge Trechsel, I'm in the middle of my cross-examination. I'm entitled to finish my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We have the right to ask questions at any time, Mr. Karnavas and I ask you to respect this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do respect it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't finished that line of questioning. If I were to skip over that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In my view you are misleading the witness into a direction the witness does not really realise where she's going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And I want to know of why the witness knows that the HVO painted their face in order not to be recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. And at the conclusion of this, Your Honour, Mr. President, I would like to have a session outside the presence of the witness. I believe we need to resolve some issues, and I think we have come to a critical stage of the proceedings where many of us, if not all of us in this thing, in this proceeding, believe we're not getting a fair trial based on the comments you've made Judge Trechsel, and I think you will find out that there is a universal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you would like to know why HVO soldiers had painted faces. There are only two solutions. Either it was so that they wouldn't be recognised by the soldiers. Then you should ask the witness whether she recognised any HVO soldiers. You didn't do that. And my colleague quite rightly then noted that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You put the question a certain way. And I also wanted to intervene, because either these HVO soldiers who entered the village were soldiers that she knew or not. She said that other inhabitants of the village knew them because they went to that cafe she spoke of. She has already answered the question. I understand you want to clarify something, but ask her whether she personally knew HVO soldiers. We'll understand things better then. We're not trying to prevent you from conducting your cross-examination, but we have to make sure that the witness isn't being manipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The word manipulation is rather strong and I take umbrage to Judge Trechsel accusing me of trying to misrepresent anything or to confuse a witness. This line of questioning goes back to your line of questioning, Mr. President, earlier on, when the witness speculated as to obviously certain people recognise certain soldiers. This is a whole line of the questioning. And if I were allowed to complete my questioning in the manner which I believe I'm entitled to, then obviously Judge Trechsel would perhaps see that I'm not trying to manipulate or misrepresent anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one is denying you this right. You have the right to cross-examine, but we have to make sure that witnesses answer questions in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in 25 years of practising law I've never had a Judge accuse me of trying to manipulate or misrepresent the truth. So I'll now leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you indicated that you didn't recognise these soldiers; correct? You did not recognise those soldiers with the painted faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You do not know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't know who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. No manipulation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam, the HVO soldiers who entered the village -- we believe that you were in that village -- or you had been in that village for one month, and before the 5th of January it seems that things were calm. As far as you can remember, before the 5th of January, did you see any HVO soldiers entering the village, moving around, or leaving, or were there no HVO members entering the village prior to that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how to answer that question. I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is simple. Prior to the 5th of January, did you personally see any HVO soldiers entering the village before the 5th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No soldiers. That's very precise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence asked you, and quite rightly, whether you had recognised any soldiers. You said that you hadn't. You didn't know any of them. But a while ago you said that there were inhabitants of the village who knew the HVO soldiers. Is this what they told you when you spoke to them? How is it that you knew about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, after everything was over, they said that they knew these men. They knew these members of the HVO who had entered the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say "they said." Who does "they" refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Muslim people. They said they knew the Croats and the HVO members who had entered the village. They had recognised quite a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You weren't surprised, since they had painted their faces black?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. They weren't surprised, because they'd spent time with them and given the way they looked, their names, well, there were quite a few of them that they were able to recognise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And you have said or at least given to understand that it was your opinion that the shelling came from the HVO. What is the reason on which you base this statement? Was there any specific reason why you thought it was the HVO who had shelled Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness. My name is Senka Nozica. I have a number of questions for you. When you arrived in Hrasnica, as far as I have understood, your mother, your sister-in-law and two brothers accompanied you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where did your two brothers go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My two brothers went before the HVO arrived, when the Serbs had started everything. Our army was heading in the direction of Bugojno, to the lines, to Prusac, near Bugojno. They were there all the time. They weren't in Hrasnica when all of this took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your two brothers, as far as I have understood you, went to the front line in Bugojno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So why do we say they went? Did they go to Hrasnica with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My elder brother just took us to Hrasnica and put us up there, but they were down there all the time, because there were a lot of Serbs there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this an assumption or do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you know that they spent their time fighting again the Serbs in Bugojno while you were in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd just like to briefly go back to something that I believe is important in your statement. Item 10, it concerns --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought you were going to put this question to the witness, but since you haven't, I'll put the question to the witness. Your brothers, were they ABiH members, or were they members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were members of the armija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't speculate if you don't know the answer, but which unit within the ABiH were they members of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I can't answer that question precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: With regard to these two individuals who were killed, you told the Prosecution that the result of the shelling Muminovic and Sejo Guric were killed. Is that what you said? And are you amending that now, or were you misunderstood at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was misunderstood when I first say this. When I first gave my statement, I said that Asim and Sejo Guric were together. And as far as Muminovic is concerned, he wasn't nearby. And I don't know what happened to him exactly. His brother appeared rapidly and said that he had been killed, but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, I'd like to point out that you then said that two individuals were killed as a result of the shelling, Muminovic, whose name we don't know, and Sejo Guric. And two or three sentences later you said, "Two individuals in our group were wounded, Zijad Sehic and Asim Guric, and I was wounded by shrapnel in the forehead." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Asim Guric about this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Today you said, it's page 17, 14 to 15 of your testimony today, you said Asim Guric knew those people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How did you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, after we were released, I saw Asim Guric in Bugojno when he was in hospital. I went there and he said that he knew those men. And when they start saying that they knew those men, well, that's what they said. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You've confused me. A minute ago when I asked you whether you had ever spoken to Asim Guric about that event you said no, and now it seems that you did speak to him in Bugojno when he was in hospital. Could you tell me when this happened exactly? Was it half a year or a year after the event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was when we were exchanged. That's when I went there to visit him and I saw him. I asked him whether he knew who it was or not, and he said, "I know them well." He told me their names, but I can't remember the names. I can't speak about things I don't know about correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before this hearing, did you perhaps meet Asim Guric a week before coming to The Hague? Did you see him? Did you meet him perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you speak to him after you had seen him in the hospital about this event that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you were wounded, as you said, in your statement you said that HVO members provided all of you with first aid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In your statement, you also said that when you were put up in the nearby village of Trnovaca, on the following day Muslims arrived. My colleague asked you about this. They came from the neighbouring houses and asked for permission that you be put up in the houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that's actually what happened later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And in your statement you said, when explaining the situation in the village with regard to armed individuals, you said that some were outside their houses. Later you said they were about 50 metres outside the houses. I'm talking about the inhabitants of the village of ABiH members of Muslims -- about Muslims from Hrasnica, and you said that some of these armed individuals were in the houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not all of them. Some were there outside and some were inside in the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was anyone inside the house you were in, any of those armed individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Which point in time are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about the time when HVO members came and asked us to leave the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about that time. I'm asking you about that one-week period. Did any of the armed ABiH members stay in the house during that seven-day period in which you were accommodated with those civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a few of them. Sometimes they would come to eat.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To eat or perhaps they opened fire from that house. Did they open fire from that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no one opened fire from that house and it wasn't possible to hit anything with a rifle from that house in which there were ABiH members.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, how do you know what the targets were and what ABiH members had to hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the targets were, but in the house that I was in, well, there were no ABiH members in the vicinity, and I know that they couldn't have done anything from that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But did they have trenches? It's obvious that you're well-informed. When you say they couldn't have done anything from there, well, do you know whether they could have done certain things and what they could have hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they didn't have trenches. They didn't have the trenches they should have had. I don't know how to put this. I don't know whether you know how these interconnecting trenches work. They didn't dig these trenches out. They had sandbags. That's what they used for shelter as far as they know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, how do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on we returned. Well, we'd go to collect food in Hrasnica and we'd see these sandbags, so that's how I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, did you know everyone, all the inhabitants of Hrasnica? A list was shown to you a minute ago, and you said that you mostly knew everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I used to go and see a relative there, and I knew all those inhabitants of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At that time when you set off in these columns of civilians and when -- and columns of soldiers, who were the other refugees like you who weren't from Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were other refugees, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So on the list you were shown, there were also individuals from other villages, not just from Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Among the fighters were there individuals from other places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because there were these refugees from Bugojno, and they were all civilians. They all set off towards Bugojno. They didn't linger in Hrasnica. The soldiers didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, none of these soldiers on the list that was shown to you was from anywhere else apart from Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Hopic Hamid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Jareb Irfan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Capalo Besim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Galecic Enes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Isakovic Dzevad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know Guric Muhamed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All these individuals were from Hrasnica as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a follow-up question. You said that you had been exchanged, prisoners had been exchanged. Does this mean that you believe you were a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why did you believe that you were a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I couldn't go anywhere, or I was only able to go to get food. We were imprisoned in the premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that when you were wounded you were cured, treated, helped by HVO soldiers. Does that mean that HVO soldiers who were there provided you with medical aid, medical aid treatment of some kind? Can you tell us how they assisted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, an HVO member gave me a bandage so that I could bandage my wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kovacic, you have the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam. I have just a couple of questions to clear up a few points that I find have not been cleared up sufficiently. For the record, page 24, line 20, you said that Asim Guric, when he was wounded, was taken to hospital by UNPROFOR; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Madam, did you see this with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So while the civilians and soldiers were all there together, the UNPROFOR arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The UNPROFOR arrived, and they took Asim Guric away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We heard testimony, I won't mention the name to avoid closed session, Your Honour. We heard direct testimony to the effect that in addition to other BH soldiers, Asim Guric walked to the next village from where, by buses or trucks, they were transported to Gornji Vakuf, the furniture factory, and that he was given first aid there. So did he talk to another village in a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Asim Guric was straight away transported to Bugojno, because UNPROFOR arrived just then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Regarding the shelling that you told us about that -- for about seven days you said there was shelling, especially when you explained that you didn't know how Muminovic was wounded, but judging from what you said, it would appear that the village was still being shelled when the HVO soldiers had already entered the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When they entered the village, the shelling stopped. They were told not to continue shelling, and the shelling stopped. But there was shooting with light weapons. That continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you've explained to me now that the shelling stopped only when the soldiers of the army and the civilians had surrendered. I don't know how long this lasted. Was it half an hour or two hours? Had the HVO soldiers already entered the village? How long did this take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, because we were at the end of the village, and the first soldiers entered at the other end, and then they went from one house to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So as HV soldiers were advancing through the village, the artillery fire continued.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It went on until we all surrendered. There wasn't a lot of it, but there was some.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see whether there were any victims of the shelling among HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear or see anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell me, madam, in your statement, in paragraph 7 you said that you came with your family from your (redacted) -- oh dear, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I mentioned the name of the village. This should be deleted. Yes, it is in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can it be redacted. Please have the name of the village redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you came from your village to Hrasnica. That is, from the region of Bugojno. You also told us that you came with members of your immediate family, but you were not the only people who had come from Bugojno municipality to this area. Other people had come too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly how many, 100, 200, 500? Some rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There weren't that many, but there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And as I can see from your statement, this was in October, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement and in your testimony also, you referred to the uniforms of the HVO. Among those you call HVO soldiers, did you see black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some, but not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the village we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did they have any different insignia, if you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I didn't pay attention to the insignia. I just saw when I was wounded there were some in camouflage uniforms and some in black uniforms. I didn't pay attention to their insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also told us, as you did in your statement, that on the 5th of January the HVO started the shooting. The question is: Who started it? You told us there were BH army members in the village, that the HVO was attacking the village. How do you know who started the shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know when the shells reached the village. It couldn't have come from our army. They didn't have any artillery, nor could they have started the shooting at our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let's go step by step. You said at first there was an exchange of rifle fire; is that right? And then later as things developed, artillery fire started too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you also said that you were sure the army in the village didn't have any heavier weapons than rifles, no artillery or howitzers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, they didn't have any such weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to the beginning. In the view of the fact that you confirmed there was an exchange of rifle fire between the HVO and the army because there were no other forces there, how do you know who started this exchange of fire? Did you yourself see the first shot or shots being fired in -- from outside the village, which would be the HVO shooting at the village or vice versa? Do you know with certainty who first started it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know because the HVO started first, because where I was living the first shots came from Pavic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you know this from your own knowledge and not from hearsay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from hearsay, because I happened to be outside when the first shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And from that moment on, this exchange continued uninterrupted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On page 32, in answer to the Presiding Judge, you said -- or you explained that it was only after the events that you heard from other villagers that members of the HVO who entered the village were also local people, local Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Madam, you didn't say this in your first statement from 1994. You don't mention that anywhere. So my question is the following: Did you tell the investigators when your statement was taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could I interrupt. You've been referring to a statement from 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I meant the 2004. I'm sure you understood the statement that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So my question is: When you spoke to the investigators and when you gave this statement that you identified today, did you ever say anything to the effect that you recognised those HVO members yourself or that you learnt from others about their identity later on, from others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't recognise them, but I heard from others that they were from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you didn't tell that to the investigators in 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. I didn't know why it didn't go down in the statement. I told them what I'm telling you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Madam, I seem to recognise a certain contradiction. Maybe you can -- can clarify. You have said that in the village of Hrasnica, all three parts included, there were only two houses of Croats, and now you say that the attackers, the HVO, who entered Hrasnica were from that village. Now, if there were only two houses, that could only have been two, three, maybe four HVO, but there must have been more, I suppose. How do you bring this together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People who had left Hrasnica before that, Pavic Polje is nearby, Volari. So there were people who used to live there. Maybe for a year before that event only two Croat houses remained. However, they knew each other. They recognised each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you then saying that only two Croat houses remained in January, 1993, while there had been more before at earlier times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in the conflict but before that. I don't know how many years before the event they had left, but for the past couple of years there were only two households there. But before that there were more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have two technical questions to ask, that is, the population census from 1981, which is still valid, which was valid, and it says there is Hrasnica listed there. So I'd like the witness to be shown this list and for this list to be placed on the ELMO, please. And in the meantime I would have a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Bugojno hospital where you visited this gentleman, was this an HVO hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please have a look. So the hospital belonged to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. I don't know. As far as I know, there was no BH army there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So please say you don't know, rather than saying no it wasn't and then say, "I don't know." Was it an HVO hospital? Do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, please have a look at this paper and see the total number of inhabitants in Hrasnica, the number of Muslims and the number of Croats in Hrasnica. Underlined. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can you clear up the picture a little?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The total number of inhabitants, then Croats, and then Muslims. Can you read these three figures for us, please? Hrasnica. Can you read it now? We didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five hundred and forty-seven.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And how many Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two hundred and eighty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two hundred and sixty-three. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted into evidence as a document, please. Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has the Prosecution any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions. I don't know if -- Your Honours, if you want me to do that now. I'm looking at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. Hurry so that we can have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked a question about the mosque, and in answer to that question, you said that the mosque in Hrasnica was damaged by the shelling; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 13, you said that when you returned to Hrasnica while you were in Trnovaca to get food from the houses, you say that you could see that the mosque in the village was destroyed. Now, my question is: Was the damage to the mosque when you returned to Hrasnica, was that different than the damage that you had seen during the time that the mosque was shelled as you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may be wrong, but I don't think this question was raised in the cross-examination. So this is additional examination in relation to the statement. Yes, my learned friend did raise the issue but in a different sense. So the Prosecution is going back to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you've heard the question. Could you give an answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was damaged at the beginning, but when we came from Trnovaca, then I saw that the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So the damage was different from what you first saw when it was shelled than the damage when you -- when you came back to Hrasnica after having been in Trnovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused. When we -- when I went to fetch food in Hrasnica from Trnovaca, when I went there for the last time I saw that the mosque was totally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, on behalf of the Judges, we thank you for coming to testify. I wish you a safe journey home. Before leaving the courtroom, I'm going to ask the registrar to pull down the blinds, and we're going to have a 30-minute break. So we will resume the hearing at a quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, will you please stand? I'm going to ask you to give us your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Senada Basic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you give us your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 29th of August, 1960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you currently employed, and what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not employed. I am a housewife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you testified, madam, before in a national or international court about the facts that occurred in your country in the 1990s, or is this for you the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time for me to testify in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please read the solemn declaration that is going to be given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. You may be seated. Will the usher remove the screen around you, please. Madam, a few points of information regarding the proceedings here. You have already met, I assume, the Prosecutor, and you will first be answering questions put to you by her. The Prosecutor has an envisaged an hour and a half for the examination-in-chief, so you will be answering her questions first.
